name: Chesapeake Bay Trust Anne Arundel County Watershed Restoration and Forestry Grant Program
summary: Grants in Anne Arundel County, Maryland for watershed restoration design and implementation, reforestation and permanent protection of forested land. Funded with Anne Arundel County and the City of Annapolis.

geography.label: Anne Arundel County, Maryland, including the City of Annapolis

steps: Pre-application site visit with the Trust
Get Trust approval before applying above the track’s funding level

documents: Landowner Letter of Commitment if the applicant does not own the site
Track 2 photographs of the restoration site
Track 2 map of the drainage area and impervious surfaces

status.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline is Friday, February 26, 2027 at 4PM ET

deadline.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline is Friday, February 26, 2027 at 4PM ET

applicant_types.quote: Who can apply: Non-profit organizations, land Trusts, land conservancies, community/homeowners' associations, faith-based organizations, and more.

geography.quote: Implementation project location: Anne Arundel County, Maryland INCLUDING the City of Annapolis.

window.quote: Program Status: OPEN Deadline is Friday, February 26, 2027 at 4PM ET

co_finance_required.quote: Match is encouraged, but not required.

effort.quote: The Trust requires that all applicants conduct a pre-application site visit with the Trust by February 12, 2027.
Deadline is Friday, February 26, 2027 at 4PM ET
Applicants interested in requests exceeding the general funding levels outlined above must discuss their project with the Trust prior to submission to receive approval to apply for a larger request.
Each application is reviewed by a Technical Review Committee (TRC)
The TRC then recommends a suite of applications to the Trust’s Board of Trustees.

documents.quote: Landowner permission through a Letter of Commitment to access the site and implement the project, if project is on land not owned by the applicant
a conceptual site plan sketch, and a photo(s) of the restoration site must be included.
Include a map of the drainage area that the proposed design will treat which delineates the location of impervious surfaces
The “Best Management Practices Worksheet” in Appendix F of the RFP

eligibility.quote: applicants for Tracks 1, 2, 3, and 6 must be certified 501(c) non-profit organizations, except for homeowners or community associations located in the City of Annapolis.
Applications for Tracks 1, 2, 3, and 6 must include at least one partner that represents a stakeholder group based in Anne Arundel County.

All projects proposed shall be voluntary. Any projects that are required under an existing or pending regulatory process or permit, are required for mitigation, or are required by a regulatory authority for any other reason
Track 1 – Watershed Planning (City of Annapolis only): requests up to $75,000
Both an Executive Officer and a Project Leader, two separate individuals, must be identified for all applications.
Project Timeline: Projects must be completed within two years upon receipt of the award. Requests to extend project completion period will be reviewed and considered on a case-by-case basis.
If a PCE will not be obtained for your proposed project, the landowner must agree to sign a long-term protection agreement.
This track allows applicants to request funding to support stormwater BMPs and afforestation/reforestation efforts at a shared project site in one request.

after_award.quote: If approved, the Trust will send an award agreement with award conditions and due dates of status, progress, and final reports.

eligibility.rule: Tracks 1–3 and 6 community groups: certified 501(c), except Annapolis community and homeowners’ associations
Tracks 1–3 and 6 watershed, community, service, youth, civic or faith groups: Anne Arundel stakeholder partner
Project is voluntary and is not required by a permit, mitigation obligation or regulator
Track 1 projects are in the City of Annapolis
Names a separate Executive Officer and Project Leader
Completes the project within two years of award unless the Trust approves an extension
Track 5 landowner agrees to long-term protection if a permanent conservation easement will not be obtained
Track 6 combines stormwater restoration and forest planting at the same site
